units.quote:
L’examen du tableau 4, plus particulièrement des rapports relatifs à la période après 
aménagement, permet de constater que les débits de pointe sont fortement écrêtés et que le 
volume de crue diminue significativement. Les temps de montée et de base crues sont 
également affectés par l’aménagement et sont multipliés quasiment par deux. (English: Examination of Table 4, particularly the ratios relative to the post-treatment period, shows that peak discharges are strongly clipped and flood volume decreases significantly. The rise and base times of the floods are also affected by the treatment and are almost multiplied by two.)

relationship.outcome_raw: envelope flood hydrograph at the outlet (maximum discharge at each time step over all floods of the period): peak discharge strongly clipped, flood volume decreased, rise and base times markedly lengthened after treatment

context.practice_as_described: Integrated anti-erosion catchment treatment ('aménagement anti-érosif intégré') of the 7.74 km2 Oued Ez-Zioud mountain catchment, Djebel Semmama, central Tunisia (semi-arid, ~350 mm rain), built 1987-1989 with finishing work to October 1993: dry-stone contour bunds ('cordons pierreux isohypses' / 'murets en pierres sèches') laid on the contour that progressively form terraces, covering 60% of the catchment on the steepest slopes; active gullies treated with stone sills and micro-dams (porous stone check structures, some gabions); some bench terraces ('banquettes') on the slopes; and the WHOLE catchment closed to grazing ('mise en défens') from 1987 (pp9-10). BASELINE (comparator): the same catchment before treatment, two pre-treatment periods 1976-1981 (17 floods) and 1982-1986 (26 floods) vs the post-treatment period 1990-1994 (14 floods); floods measured at the outlet gauge (before-after design, no control catchment).
context.note: Tableau 4 'Comparaison des paramètres des hydrogrammes enveloppes' (p11): the table values are not in the text layer, so the size of the peak reduction cannot be encoded from this page. The near-doubling refers to rise and base time, not peak size; strength left unspecified. 'Significantly' here is the authors' rule of a relative difference above 10% (p4), not a statistical test. Supersedes the second-hand reading in ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s / ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_2 (Roose 2006 paraphrase).

units.citation: Barron et al. (2005). Run-off water harvesting for dry spell mitigation in maize (Zea mays L.): results from on-farm research in semi-arid Kenya. Agricultural Water Management.
units.quote:
The poor rainfall received in SR98 generated
very little run-off, and the earth dam barely contained any water.

relationship.outcome_raw: earth-dam function in the SR98 drought season: the catchment generated very little runoff and the dam held almost no water to supply

context.practice_as_described: surface run-off from a 2.7 ha catchment harvested in a hand-dug, tarpaulin-lined earth dam (300 m3) and supplied by gravity as supplemental irrigation (SI) to mitigate dry spells in maize on existing in-situ terraces; urea N at 0, 30 or 80 kg N/ha and 12 kg P/ha superphosphate on all plots; control NI0 = farmers' practice (no SI, no N)
context.note: asset function (water supply), not structural damage: the authors classify SR98 as one of two "complete drought seasons" (p17); the dam "harvested sufficient amounts of water for SI treatment, except during complete drought season as SR98" (p18) | Pete 2026-10-19 ruling wh_supplemental_irrigation (A+C), applied 2026-10-29: runoff capture IS water harvesting, the yield is delivered through irrigation, so the unit is tagged bundled with irrigation (bundle discount applies).

units.quote: tre estas tecnologias, o uso da irrigação de salvação tem reduzido os riscos da exploração agrícola em anos cuja precipitação pluviométrica é irregular, proporcionando até duas colheitas em anos considerados normais de chuvas. Segundo Porto et al. (1983), no Semi-Árido brasi- leiro, três em cada dez anos são considerados normais com relação à quantidade e à distribuição das chuvas. Define-se a irrigação de salvação como a lâmina de água aplicada à cul- tura nos veranicos que comumente ocorrem durante o período chuvoso na região Nordeste, de forma a não permitir que a cultura sofra estresse hídrico e, em alguns casos, morra. No Semi-Árido brasileiro, após as pri- meiras chuvas, é comum ocorrerem períodos de 20 a 30 dias sem novas chuvas, comprometendo seriamente a germinação e outras fases de de- senvolvimento das culturas. (English: [Am]ong these technologies, supplemental (salvation) irrigation has reduced the risks of farming in years with irregular rainfall, allowing up to two harvests in years considered normal. According to Porto et al. (1983), in the Brazilian semi-arid three in every ten years are considered normal in rainfall quantity and distribution. Salvation irrigation is defined as the depth of water applied to the crop during the dry spells (veranicos) that commonly occur during the rainy season in the Northeast, so as not to let the crop suffer water stress and, in some cases, die. In the Brazilian semi-arid, after the first rains, periods of 20 to 30 days without new rain are common, seriously compromising germination and other crop development phases.)

The overall sustainability indices for 10 year time period, with increasing series of 
concurrent below average rainfall years, does not show strong differences as the drought

periods (Figure 6-10).  Overall the resilience index is low, but it shows some change,

not present in the system in the analysis in section 6.3.1.

units.quote:
The findings (Fig. 4d and Supplementary Table 2) suggest robust 
programme impacts in the event of a moderate drought, with signif-
icant buffering effects captured by both EVI and GOSIF-GPP.

relationship.outcome_raw: drought impact on land productivity under moderate drought, treated vs control watersheds

context.practice_as_described: Ethiopia's Sustainable Land Management Project phase 1 (SLMP1) in 45 critically degraded highland watersheds: 'building small-scale irrigation projects, constructing surface water-harvesting systems for smallholder farming communities, reducing livestock overgrazing of hillsides, afforestation or reforestation of degraded areas and rehabilitating gullies'
context.note: satellite (MODIS EVI 1 km, GOSIF-GPP 5 km) difference-in-differences with pipeline design: SLMP1 watersheds (treated) vs SLMP2 watersheds (control), main (Meher) crop season 2002-2015, cropland/rangeland pixels above 1,000 m; drought defined by SPI. Water harvesting is one of five listed programme measures and its share is not reported; outcome is land productivity (EVI/GPP), which the authors state is not equivalent to crop yield. Mechanism: the paper identifies the programme effect causally but does not isolate which measure buffers drought (drought reduced productivity in both groups, reductions remarkably lower in treated areas, p3). Normal-year reference: no EVI increase and +3.08% GPP in drought-free areas.

units.citation: Fox et al. (2005). Risk analysis and economic viability of water harvesting for supplemental irrigation in semi-arid Burkina Faso and Kenya. Agricultural Systems.
units.quote:
The probability of drought is 0.1 and cannot be mitigated since there is insuﬃcient
amount of water available for harvesting and hence for SI. Seventy-ﬁve per cent of
the severe dry spells can be partly mitigated with SI, but not fully as they occur late
in the rainy season (during ﬂowering and grain ﬁlling) and require a minimum of
three SI applications. As the WH system can only support two SI applications,
the dry spell is only partly mitigated, transforming the severe dry spell to mild dry
spells. Field experience indicate that all of the mild dry spells can be mitigated, ex-
plaining the increased occurrence of zero stress from P ¼ 0:1 in control treatment
to P ¼ 0:5 in SI treatment.

units.quote:
The results showed that tied rides had a signiﬁcantly higher (P <0.05) moisture
content in the 0–5 and 6–10 cm depth compared to conventional system, while there
were no signiﬁcant differences between the two tillage systems at 11–15 cm (Fig. 4).
The results indicated that tied ridges had signiﬁcantly higher percentage of
moisture content at 0–5 and 6–10 but not at 11–15 cm. Higher moisture content at
0–5 cm illustrates the effectiveness of tied contours in moisture conservation on top
soil horizons. The 2018–2019 season was a drought year in Zimbabwe, so the effects
of the tillage method on moisture was apparent.

relationship.outcome_raw: topsoil moisture content (top two sampling depths) under tied contour ridges vs conventional tillage, cotton field trial, drought season; no difference at the deepest sampled layer

context.practice_as_described: Tied contour ridges (ridges with cross-ties that trap rain where it falls; in-field moisture harvesting) under six cotton genotypes. BASELINE: conventional tillage (ploughing without ridges) with the same genotypes.
context.note: Factorial field trial: two tillage systems x six cotton genotypes (QM301, CRIM 51 local; M579, M577, M567, M52 imported from India). This unit is the tillage main effect, so the ridge effect is not bundled with the new varieties. Fig. 4 (p10) 'Effects of tillage system on percentage moisture content at three sampling depths' shows values only as bars: no numbers quotable. Deepest layer (11-15 cm) not significant. Only season 2018-2019, which p3 describes as 'below normal and highly erratic and patchy rainfall' with crops 'written off because of prolonged dryness' (citing FEWS Net 2019). Book chapter reporting a primary trial with thin methods (no site, plot size or replication stated). Abstract says 'water harvesting in form of planting basins' raised boll number; the body tests tied ridges only - inconsistency flagged.
